bounds.domain: One app, one provision child on its last allowed attempt, one immutable generation and one possible replacement generation. Parent admission, placement publication and exact execution fencing are premises. A successful READY write records the current app result independently of the child job's acknowledgement.
bounds.persistence: The job failure and any eligible app failure are one database transaction. The original tenant and generation must match. Only building and deploying are eligible for the app failure write. Expiry abstracts loss of the original job lease and eligibility for stale exhaustion. No late execution can settle after expiry.
bounds.conformance: The maintained PGlite suite executes the actual job service, leases, running placement, READY writer, public status projection and terminal failure callback. A fixture throws only after reading the committed READY result. An ingress failure before READY still records app ERROR with the running placement preserved. Docker and ingress responses are fixture inputs.
bounds.gaps: Bounded to the app failure writeback after the child handoff. Direct terminal exhaustion is exercised in the two new PGlite cases. Expired recovery shares the callback and is abstracted by the model. Job status can report failed when ancillary completion is unconfirmed. External reachability, ingress repair, cache acknowledgement, full lease recovery and retry composition are outside the proof.

assumptions: The job and dependent writeback commit together under the existing lease, tenant and generation authority. No fairness is assumed.
The exhausted error or expired lease remains observable and its database transaction is continuously eligible. The matching settlement or stale recovery is weakly fair.
No fairness is assumed. An eligible terminal transaction can remain unscheduled.
